name: Scribe
description: The LaTeX editor for working scientists. Paper, notebooks and figures in one project, compiled on your machine.
readme_summary: Scribe is a desktop LaTeX editor designed for scientists, integrating LaTeX papers with Python notebooks and figures into a single project. It allows for seamless compilation of documents on the user's machine using Tectonic or TeX Live, ensuring privacy and local control.
key_features: Integrated LaTeX paper editing with Python notebooks and figures
Local compilation using Tectonic or TeX Live
CodeMirror 6 editor with LaTeX-specific features (completion, snippets, hover info)
Support for TikZ diagrams
Track changes, comments, and revision management
Reference management and note-taking capabilities
Cross-platform desktop application built with Tauri
primary_use_case: A unified environment for scientists to write research papers, embed dynamic content from Python notebooks, and manage all related assets locally.
cover_image_prompt: A scientist in a cozy, well-lit study, looking at a large, open book on a desk. The book's pages seamlessly transition from elegant LaTeX code on the left to a dynamic, colorful scientific graph and a detailed diagram on the right. Small, glowing particles representing data flow from a miniature, stylized Python notebook icon towards the graph. The scientist is holding a quill that subtly glows with a digital aura. The repository name 'Scribe' is elegantly embossed on the book's cover. The overall mood is one of focused creation and seamless integration. Rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style with a warm, inviting color palette and clear, crisp details.

name: OpenTV-Remote
description: Free, open-source smart TV remote for Android and iPhone. Custom layouts, local Wi-Fi control, and English/Russian interfaces. MIT licensed.
readme_summary: OpenTV-Remote is a free, open-source mobile application for Android and iPhone that functions as a smart TV remote. It offers custom layouts, local Wi-Fi control, and supports English and Russian languages, with a focus on providing a seamless and user-friendly remote experience without requiring subscriptions or accounts.
key_features: Free and open-source (MIT License)
No subscription, ads, or account required
Automatic network discovery
Saved TVs and capability-aware controls
Customizable layouts and eight visual templates
Support for English and Russian languages
Native Android (Kotlin/Jetpack Compose) and iPhone (SwiftUI) apps
Local Wi-Fi control
Pointer support via native TV provider or Android Bluetooth HID
primary_use_case: To provide users with a free, open-source, and highly customizable smart TV remote control application for their Android and iPhone devices, enabling local network control of various smart TVs.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, friendly robot holding a universal remote control, with glowing lines of Wi-Fi signals emanating from the remote and connecting to various smart TV icons floating in the background. The robot is smiling, and the scene is set against a clean, modern backdrop with subtle digital patterns. Small, intuitive icons representing different TV brands and functions (like play, pause, volume) are subtly integrated into the scene. The overall mood is helpful and accessible, emphasizing ease of use and broad compatibility. The repository name 'OpenTV-Remote' is subtly displayed on the robot's chest or on a small digital screen within the scene. 3D isometric illustration style with vibrant, friendly colors and soft lighting.

name: codeburn
description: Free, local tool to track AI coding token usage and cost across 37 tools and agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini and more), by model, project, and task. npx codeburn
readme_summary: CodeBurn is a free, local tool designed to track AI coding token usage and associated costs across numerous AI tools and agents. It provides detailed breakdowns by model, project, and task, offering visibility into AI spending.
key_features: Tracks AI coding token usage and cost
Supports 37 AI tools and agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini)
Provides breakdowns by model, project, and task
Offers both a CLI and a menubar/web dashboard interface
Local and free to use
primary_use_case: To provide developers with clear visibility and control over their AI coding tool token consumption and associated costs.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old owl, perched on a branch made of glowing code, meticulously sorting and tallying colorful, translucent orbs representing AI tokens. Each orb is labeled with a different AI tool's icon (like a stylized Claude, Cursor, or Gemini logo). The owl's eyes glow with a soft light, illuminating a ledger book open below it, which displays clear, simple charts and figures showing token counts and costs for different projects. Subtle digital particles flow from the orbs to the ledger. The background is a soft, abstract representation of a digital landscape. The overall mood is one of clarity and insight. Style: 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a warm, inviting color palette.

name: open-source-games
description: A list of open source games.
readme_summary: This repository is a curated list of open-source video games and open-source remakes of commercial games. It categorizes these games by genre, providing links to their respective websites and source code repositories.
key_features: Curated list of open-source games
Categorization by genre
Links to game websites
Links to source code repositories
Includes remakes of commercial games
primary_use_case: Discovering and accessing open-source video games and their source code.
cover_image_prompt: A vibrant, open book lies on a wooden desk, with each page transforming into a portal to a different game world. One portal shows a pixelated spaceship, another a bustling city, and a third a character in a fantasy landscape. Glowing lines of code emanate from the book, connecting the portals and forming the repository name 'Open Source Games' subtly in the background. The scene is illuminated by a warm, inviting light, suggesting discovery and play. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with rich textures and clear, distinct game representations.

name: OpenGait
description: A flexible and extensible framework for gait recognition. You can focus on designing your own models and comparing with state-of-the-arts easily with the help of OpenGait.
readme_summary: OpenGait is a flexible and extensible Python framework for gait recognition, enabling researchers to design and compare state-of-the-art models. It supports various datasets and has been highlighted in CVPR2023 and TPAMI2025.
key_features: Flexible and extensible framework
Gait recognition model design and comparison
Support for multiple datasets (GaitLU-1M, SUSTech1K, etc.)
Integration of advanced models (FoundationGait, BiggerGait, DenoisingGait, etc.)
Published research in top-tier conferences (CVPR, TPAMI, ECCV, NeurIPS, MICCAI, AAAI)
primary_use_case: Developing, training, and evaluating custom gait recognition models.
cover_image_prompt: A master tailor meticulously crafting unique suits from raw fabric. Each suit represents a different gait recognition model, with the tailor using advanced digital tools and blueprints (subtly showing code snippets and data visualizations) to precisely measure and assemble the garments. The raw fabric symbolizes diverse human movements, and the finished suits, each distinct yet clearly identifiable by their unique 'cut' (gait signature), are displayed on mannequins. The scene is a bright, modern workshop with a clean, organized aesthetic, emphasizing precision and customization. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear iconography and a vibrant, yet professional color palette, with the 'OpenGait' logo subtly integrated into the workshop signage.
